setup-mfa.title: Two-Factor Authentication
setup-mfa.description: Enter the verification code from your authenticator app.

setup-cameras.title: Select Cameras
setup-cameras.description: Choose which cameras from your CuboAI account to add. Nothing is added automatically — you can change this later in the integration Options.

setup-options.title: Configure CuboAI Integration
setup-options.description: Configure the alert and download behavior for your CuboAI cameras.

fields.label: Enable debug logs
fields.help: Turn on when reporting an issue. Writes full diagnostics for the whole integration: `cuboai_debug.log` (config folder, all integration messages), `custom_components/cuboai/bin/go2rtc.log` (streaming engine), `cuboai_last_alert_debug.log` (alerts), plus debug messages in the Home Assistant log. Log files rotate at 2 MB. Redact camera credentials before sharing — see the [debugging guide]({docs_url}).

fields.label: RTSP port for the local camera stream
fields.help: Port for the integration's own streaming engine. It self-heals — if the port you pick is already taken, it moves to the next free one automatically. Home Assistant's built-in go2rtc normally already uses 8555, so a default of 8557 here is expected and not an error.

fields.label: Number of alerts to retain in state attributes
Maximum number of downloaded photos to keep
Time window to check for alerts (hours)
Make your first camera available to UniFi Protect (ONVIF)
fields.help: Lets UniFi Protect find your first camera and add it as a third-party camera. In Protect, either turn on Settings → System → Discover Third-Party Cameras, or add it by address (shown as unifi_protect_address on its WebRTC Stream sensor). A Cubo 3 sends H.265, which Protect passes to viewers unconverted: turn on 'Transcode these cameras to H.264' for it in Configure if a phone or browser shows no picture. More cameras can be added later in Configure.

fields.label: UniFi Protect password
fields.help: Type this same username and password into Protect when it asks. Protect will not add a camera without a password.

fields.label: Notify me when the streaming engine restarts
fields.help: The streaming engine is restarted automatically if it stops unexpectedly. Leave this on to be told when that happens — a crash used to be completely silent, and an engine that keeps dying is worth knowing about. Turn it off if you would rather not see the notification.

fields.label: RTSP port for the local camera stream
fields.help: Port for the integration's own streaming engine. It self-heals — if the port you pick is already taken, it moves to the next free one automatically. Home Assistant's built-in go2rtc normally already uses 8555, so a default of 8557 here is expected and not an error.

fields.label: Expose RTSP stream for NVR (shows a copyable URL on the WebRTC Stream sensor)
NVR stream password (leave EMPTY for no password — most compatible with Hikvision/HiLook)
Number of alerts to retain in state attributes
Maximum number of downloaded photos to keep
Time window to check for alerts (hours)
Transcode these cameras to H.264 (needed for HomeKit / HLS with H.265 cameras like Cubo 3)
fields.help: Check a camera only if it is H.265/HEVC (e.g. Cubo 3 / SW05) and fails in HomeKit or the HA stream view with a 'demuxing timed out' error. Leave native-H.264 cameras (Cubo 2 / CB02) unchecked — transcoding uses extra CPU.

fields.label: Size of the H.264 transcode
fields.help: 1080p keeps full HD, the most HomeKit shows. Choose 720p if the machine running Home Assistant cannot convert 1080p in real time (a Raspberry Pi 4, for example): a picture that falls behind makes HomeKit show 'No Response'. Download diagnostics to check: it says when the conversion is too slow. Applies only to the cameras checked above.

fields.label: Burn the date and time into these cameras' NVR recordings
fields.help: Only the stream an NVR records (the nvr_rtsp_url on the camera's WebRTC Stream sensor) gets the time burned into the picture. Live view and HomeKit are unchanged. Costs a transcode on this machine per checked camera.

fields.label: Make cameras available to UniFi Protect (ONVIF)
fields.help: Lets UniFi Protect find the chosen cameras and add them as third-party cameras. In Protect, either turn on Settings → System → Discover Third-Party Cameras, or add each camera by address (shown as unifi_protect_address on its WebRTC Stream sensor). Each camera gets its own port. A Cubo 3 sends H.265, which Protect passes to viewers unconverted: check 'Transcode these cameras to H.264' for it if a phone or browser shows no picture.

fields.label: Cameras to show in UniFi Protect
fields.help: Each camera appears in Protect under its name in Home Assistant. Once a camera has a port it keeps it, even if you untick it and tick it again later.

fields.label: UniFi Protect password
fields.help: Type this same username and password into Protect when it asks. Protect will not add a camera without a password.

fields.label: UniFi Protect (ONVIF) port of the first camera
fields.help: Protect remembers each camera's port when it adds it, so ports are never changed automatically. The first camera uses this port; each further camera the next free one.
